title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a Defendant's Defense on the Nature of the Act Affects the Establishment of Voluntary Surrender

articles.content_en:
March 26, 2004
Supreme People's Court
Reply on Whether a Defendant's Justification of the Nature of the Conduct
Affects the Establishment of Voluntary Surrender
Fa Shi [2004] No. 2
Higher People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region:
Your Request dated June 10, 2003 titled 'Request for Instructions on Whether a Defendant's Justification of the Nature of Facts Affects the Establishment of Surrender and Voluntary Surrender' has been received. Upon examination, the reply is as follows:
According to Article 67(1) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service, voluntarily surrendering oneself after committing a crime and truthfully confessing one's crime constitutes voluntary surrender. A defendant's justification of the nature of the conduct shall not affect the establishment of voluntary surrender.
It is hereby replied.
